Oregon :: Geography :: Climate :: chunk_0014
Main article: [Climate of Oregon](/wiki/Climate_of_Oregon "Climate of Oregon")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/Oregon_K%C3%B6ppen.svg/330px-Oregon_K%C3%B6ppen.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Oregon_K%C3%B6ppen.svg)

[Köppen climate types](/wiki/K%C3%B6ppen_climate_classification "Köppen climate classification") in Oregon

Most of Oregon has a generally mild climate, though there is significant variation given the variety of landscapes across the state.[[89]](#cite_note-91) The state's western region (west of the [Cascade Range](/wiki/Cascade_Range "Cascade Range")) has an [oceanic climate](/wiki/Oceanic_climate "Oceanic climate"), populated by dense [evergreen](/wiki/Temperate_rainforest "Temperate rainforest") mixed forests. Western Oregon's climate is heavily influenced by the Pacific Ocean; the western third of Oregon is very wet in the winter, moderately to very wet during the spring and fall, and dry during the summer. The [relative humidity](/wiki/Relative_humidity "Relative humidity") of Western Oregon is high except during summer days, which are semi-dry to semi-humid; Eastern Oregon typically sees low humidity year-round.[[90]](#cite_note-dri-92)

The state's southwestern portion, particularly the [Rogue Valley](/wiki/Rogue_Valley "Rogue Valley"), has a [Mediterranean climate](/wiki/Mediterranean_climate "Mediterranean climate") with drier and sunnier winters and hotter summers, similar to [Northern California](/wiki/Northern_California "Northern California").[[91]](#cite_note-93)

Oregon's northeastern portion has a [steppe climate](/wiki/Steppe_climate "Steppe climate"), and its high terrain regions have a [subarctic climate](/wiki/Subarctic_climate "Subarctic climate"). Like [Western Europe](/wiki/Western_Europe "Western Europe"), Oregon, and the Pacific Northwest in general, is considered warm for its latitude, and the state has far milder winters at a given elevation than comparable latitudes

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e6/Victor_Hugo_by_%C3%89tienne_Carjat_1876_-_full.jpg/250px-Victor_Hugo_by_%C3%89tienne_Carjat_1876_-_full.jpg)](/wiki/File:Victor_Hugo_by_%C3%89tienne_Carjat_1876_-_full.jpg)

[Victor Hugo](/wiki/Victor_Hugo "Victor Hugo"), a French [Romantic](/wiki/Romanticism "Romanticism") writer and politician

The earliest [French literature](/wiki/French_literature "French literature") dates from the Middle Ages, when there were several languages and dialects, and writers used their own spelling and grammar. Some authors of medieval texts, such as *[Tristan and Iseult](/wiki/Tristan_and_Iseult "Tristan and Iseult")* and *[Lancelot-Grail](/wiki/Lancelot-Grail "Lancelot-Grail"),* are unknown. Three famous medieval authors are [Chrétien de Troyes](/wiki/Chr%C3%A9tien_de_Troyes "Chrétien de Troyes"), [Christine de Pizan](/wiki/Christine_de_Pizan "Christine de Pizan") ([langue d'oïl](/wiki/Langues_d%27o%C3%AFl "Langues d'oïl")), and Duke [William IX of Aquitaine](/wiki/William_IX_of_Aquitaine "William IX of Aquitaine") ([langue d'oc](/wiki/Occitan_language "Occitan language")). Much medieval [French poetry](/wiki/French_poetry "French poetry") and literature was inspired by the legends of the [Carolingian cycle](/wiki/Matter_of_France "Matter of France"), such as the *[Song of Roland](/wiki/Song_of_Roland "Song of Roland")* and the [chansons de geste](/wiki/Chansons_de_geste "Chansons de geste"). The *Roman de Renart*, written in 1175 by Perrout de Saint Cloude, tells the story of the medieval character [Reynard](/wiki/Reynard_the_Fox "Reynard the Fox") ('the Fox') and is another example of early French writing. An important 16th-century writer was [François Rabelais](/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Rabelais "François Rabelais"), who wrote five popular early [picaresque](/wiki/Picaresque "Picaresque") novels. Rabelais was also in regular communication with [Marguerite de Navarre]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/8/84/TR_Age_11_Paris.jpg)](/wiki/File:TR_Age_11_Paris.jpg)

Roosevelt aged 11

Theodore Roosevelt Jr. was born on October 27, 1858, at [28 East 20th Street](/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt_Birthplace_National_Historic_Site "Theodore Roosevelt Birthplace National Historic Site") in [Manhattan](/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan").[[1]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris19793-2) His parents were [Martha Stewart Bulloch](/wiki/Martha_Bulloch_Roosevelt "Martha Bulloch Roosevelt") and businessman [Theodore Roosevelt Sr.](/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt_Sr. "Theodore Roosevelt Sr.") He had an older sister Anna (called [Bamie](/wiki/Bamie_Roosevelt "Bamie Roosevelt")), a younger brother [Elliott](/wiki/Elliott_Roosevelt_(socialite) "Elliott Roosevelt (socialite)"), and a younger sister [Corinne](/wiki/Corinne_Roosevelt_Robinson "Corinne Roosevelt Robinson").[[2]](#cite_note-3)

Roosevelt's youth was shaped by his poor health and debilitating asthma attacks, which terrified him and his parents. Doctors had no cure.[[3]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcCullough1981[httpsbooksgooglecombooksidnuzmvrqPvdICpgPA93_93–108]-4) Nevertheless, he was energetic and mischievously inquisitive.[[4]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPutnam195823–27-5) His lifelong interest in [zoology](/wiki/Zoology "Zoology") began at age seven when he saw a dead [seal](/wiki/Pinniped "Pinniped") at a market; after obtaining the seal's head, Roosevelt and his cousins formed the "Roosevelt Museum of Natural History". Having learned the rudiments of [taxidermy](/wiki/Taxidermy "Taxidermy"), he filled his makeshift museum with animals he killed or caught. At age nine, he recorded his observations in a paper entitled "The Natural History of Insects".[[5]](#cite_note-environment-6)

Family trips, including tours of Europe in 1869 and 1870, and [Egypt](/wiki/Khedivate_of_Egypt "Khedivate of Egypt") in 1872, shaped his cosmopolitan perspective.[[6]](#cite_note-F

The **Yellow River**,[[a]](#cite_note-1) also known as **Huanghe**, is the [second-longest river](/wiki/List_of_the_longest_rivers_of_China "List of the longest rivers of China") in China and the [sixth-longest](/wiki/List_of_rivers_by_length "List of rivers by length") river system on Earth, with an estimated length of 5,464 km (3,395 mi) and a [drainage basin](/wiki/Drainage_basin "Drainage basin") of 795,000 km2 (307,000 sq mi). Beginning in the [Bayan Har Mountains](/wiki/Bayan_Har_Mountains "Bayan Har Mountains"), the river flows generally eastwards before entering the 1,500 km (930 mi) long Ordos Loop, which runs northeast at [Gansu](/wiki/Gansu "Gansu") through the [Ordos Plateau](/wiki/Ordos_Plateau "Ordos Plateau") and turns east in [Inner Mongolia](/wiki/Inner_Mongolia "Inner Mongolia"). The river then turns sharply southwards to form the border between [Shanxi](/wiki/Shanxi "Shanxi") and [Shaanxi](/wiki/Shaanxi "Shaanxi"), turns eastwards at its confluence with the [Wei River](/wiki/Wei_River "Wei River"), and flows across the [North China Plain](/wiki/North_China_Plain "North China Plain") before emptying into the [Bohai Sea](/wiki/Bohai_Sea "Bohai Sea"). The river is named for the yellow color of its water, which comes from the large amount of sediment discharged into the water as the river flows through the [Loess Plateau](/wiki/Loess_Plateau "Loess Plateau").[[1]](#cite_note-:022-2)

The Yellow River basin was the birthplace of [ancient Chinese civilization](/wiki/Yellow_River_civilization "Yellow River civilization"). 2011 California wildfires :: Background :: chunk_0001
Further information: [List of California wildfires](/wiki/List_of_California_wildfires "List of California wildfires")

The timing of "fire season" in California is variable, depending on the amount of prior winter and spring precipitation, the frequency and severity of weather such as heat waves and wind events, and moisture content in vegetation. [Northern California](/wiki/Northern_California "Northern California") typically sees wildfire activity between late spring and early fall, peaking in the summer with hotter and drier conditions. Occasional cold frontal passages can bring wind and lightning. The timing of fire season in Southern California is similar, peaking between late spring and fall. The severity and duration of peak activity in either part of the state is modulated in part by weather events: downslope/offshore wind events can lead to critical fire weather, while onshore flow and Pacific weather systems can bring conditions that hamper wildfire growth.[[4]](#cite_note-4)[[5]](#cite_note-:02-5)

Big Tech :: Nicknames :: Magnificent Seven :: chunk_0013
A larger group known as the Magnificent Seven adds [Nvidia](/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia") and Tesla to the Big Five, based on their contributions to the S&P 500. In 2023, the Magnificent Seven accounted for approximately two-thirds of the S&P 500's gains.[[104]](#cite_note-Krauskopf_2023-105)[[105]](#cite_note-106)[[106]](#cite_note-107)[[107]](#cite_note-108) Over the course of the year, the Magnificent Seven delivered a groundbreaking 107% [return on investment](/wiki/Return_on_investment "Return on investment"), which analysts credited to the [AI boom](/wiki/AI_boom "AI boom") and expected [interest rate](/wiki/Federal_funds_rate "Federal funds rate") cuts by the [Federal Reserve](/wiki/Federal_Reserve "Federal Reserve").[[108]](#cite_note-109)

By January 2024, the Magnificent Seven accounted for 29% of the S&P 500.[[109]](#cite_note-110) In February 2024, as the Magnificent Seven approached a combined valuation of $13 trillion,[[110]](#cite_note-111) [Deutsche Bank](/wiki/Deutsche_Bank "Deutsche Bank") stated that the group exceeded the valuation of the total stock market in every country in the world except Japan, China, and the United States.[[111]](#cite_note-CNBC_2-19-2024-112)

Main article: [Stuyvesant High School](/wiki/Stuyvesant_High_School "Stuyvesant High School")

Stuyvesant High School is named after [Peter Stuyvesant](/wiki/Peter_Stuyvesant "Peter Stuyvesant"), the last [Dutch](/wiki/Dutch_Empire "Dutch Empire") governor of [New Netherland](/wiki/New_Netherland "New Netherland") before the colony was transferred to [England](/wiki/Kingdom_of_England "Kingdom of England") in 1664.[[2]](#cite_note-StuyLandmark-2) Of the nine Specialized high schools, Stuyvesant has the highest score cutoff for entry.

The school was established in 1904 as a [manual training school](/wiki/Vocational_education "Vocational education") for boys, hosting 155 students and 12 teachers. In 1907, it moved from its original location at 225 East [23rd Street](/wiki/23rd_Street_(Manhattan) "23rd Street (Manhattan)") to a building designed by [C. B. J. Snyder](/wiki/C._B._J._Snyder "C. B. J. Snyder") at 345 East 15th Street, where it remained for 85 years. It moved to its current location, a building on the Hudson River at 345 Chambers Street, in 1992.

The state flag depicts the Great Seal of Illinois, which was designed in 1819 and emulated the [Great Seal of the United States](/wiki/Great_Seal_of_the_United_States "Great Seal of the United States"). In the eagle's beak there is a banner with the state motto, "State Sovereignty, National Union." The dates on the seal, 1818 and 1868, represent the year Illinois became a state and the year in which the Great Seal was redesigned by [Sharon Tyndale](/wiki/Sharon_Tyndale "Sharon Tyndale"). Although "State Sovereignty" comes first in the motto, "State" is at the bottom and "Sovereignty" is upside-down.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

It is one of nine U.S. state flags to feature an eagle, alongside those of [Iowa](/wiki/Flag_of_Iowa "Flag of Iowa"), [Michigan](/wiki/Flag_of_Michigan "Flag of Michigan"), [Missouri](/wiki/Flag_of_Missouri "Flag of Missouri"), [New York](/wiki/Coat_of_arms_of_New_York "Coat of arms of New York"), [North Dakota](/wiki/Flag_of_North_Dakota "Flag of North Dakota"), [Oregon](/wiki/Flag_of_Oregon "Flag of Oregon"), [Pennsylvania](/wiki/Flag_of_Pennsylvania "Flag of Pennsylvania"), and [Wyoming](/wiki/Flag_of_Wyoming "Flag of Wyoming").

fanoutqa_036381.x:
Sequoia sempervirens :: Distribution and habitat :: chunk_0004
Coast redwoods occupy a narrow strip of land approximately 750 km (470 mi) in length and 8–75 km (5–47 mi) in width along the Pacific coast of North America; the most southerly native grove is in [Monterey County, California](/wiki/Monterey_County,_California "Monterey County, California"), and the most northerly groves are in extreme southwestern Oregon. The aforementioned qualification of "native" is because the species was introduced to various locations in [Victoria, Australia](/wiki/Victoria_(state) "Victoria (state)"), in the 1930s for experimental reasons and have since flourished. The prevailing native elevation range is 30–750 m (100–2,460 ft) above sea level, occasionally down to 0 and up to about 900 m (3,000 ft).[[22]](#cite_note-22) They usually grow in the mountains where precipitation from the incoming moisture off the ocean is greater. The tallest and oldest trees are found in deep valleys and gullies, where year-round streams can flow, and fog drip is regular. The [terrain](/wiki/Terrain "Terrain") also made it harder for loggers to get to the trees and to get them out after [felling](/wiki/Felling "Felling"). The trees above the fog layer, above about 700 m (2,300 ft), are shorter and smaller due to the drier, windier, and colder conditions. In addition, [Douglas-fir](/wiki/Douglas-fir "Douglas-fir"), [pine](/wiki/Pine "Pine"), and [tanoak](/wiki/Tanoak "Tanoak") often crowd out redwoods at these elevations. Few redwoods grow close to the ocean, due to intense salt spray, sand, and wind. [Coalescence](/wiki/Coalescence_(physics) "Coalescence (physics)") of coastal fog accounts for a considerable part of the trees' water needs.[[23]](#cite_note-Bionet1998-23) Fog in the 21st century is, however, reduced from what it was in the prior century, which is a problem that may be compounded by [climate change](/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change").[[24]](#cite_note-24)
